claims: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed test flight.
Artemis II is the first to the Moon since 1972.
Artemis II is designed to validate the Orion spacecraft's systems.
Artemis II is launching April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II crew includes Wiseman, Glover, Koch, and Hansen.
The Artemis II mission goal is to test the Orion capsule, its life support systems, and the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket with humans on board.
Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I flight.
The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II flight path takes the crew behind the far side of the Moon.
The Artemis II mission goes further into space than any human has traveled since 1972.
The Artemis II mission is expected to last roughly 10 days.
The Artemis II mission concludes with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II crew will test manual piloting of the Orion capsule.
The Artemis II crew will perform in-orbit inspections before returning to Earth.
The Artemis II launch site is Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The Artemis II SLS rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1.
The Artemis II crew spends the first 24+ hours checking systems in high elliptical orbit.
Artemis II Trans-Lunar Injection occurs on Day 2.
Artemis II Trans-Lunar Injection sends the crew on a figure-eight free-return trajectory around the Moon.
Artemis II Lunar Flyby occurs on Day 6.
During Artemis II Lunar Flyby, the crew conducts a close pass to the far side of the Moon.
During Artemis II Lunar Flyby, the crew photographs the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II splashdown occurs on Day 10 in the Pacific Ocean.
